design.design:
**Facts re-checked (docs opened).** OpenRouter: `models` is a priority-ordered array; with the OpenAI SDK, `model` is tried first and `extra_body.models` after; the reply's `model` says who answered. LiteLLM: `fallbacks` in the body, strings or `{model,…}` objects, tried in order; its `x-litellm-attempted-fallbacks` header is the precedent for ours. One claim was wrong: Codex's provider config has headers and query parameters but no body fields, so Codex can send neither list. Nothing outside runs (no container, image, port or download), so ARM64 is not in question.

**Code: `/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/15-routes.mjs`, about 50 lines, 16 duplicate lines removed.**
1. `callOrder(body)`: `model` (split on commas: the one new spelling, for Codex), then `models`, then `fallbacks` (a string, or an entry's `.model`). Both fields are deleted. Repeats are dropped; more than 4 names, or a non-name, is a 400.
2. One name: today's path, untouched, start-on-call included.
3. Several names: find each target as today (`sparkie` or the brain's name → `agentTarget()`/main; otherwise `runningModels(viewer)`). Not running: skip. Running: `proxyModel(…, { moveOn: true })`.
4. `proxyModel` returns false, with nothing sent, on no connection within 3 s, refused/reset, or 502/503/504. Otherwise it writes the reply with `x-spark-model: <listed name>` and, if any were skipped, `x-spark-skipped: <name> (not running)`. It marks `inUse` only then. The brain's copy of the proxy block (lines 181–197) calls it too.
5. All skipped: 503, `type: unavailable`, `Retry-After: 30`, each name and why.
6. A list never reaches `startOnCall`.

**Data, not code:**
- a `fallback` hint (the model string and the body form) in `running_models`' `gateway` result (`service/src/16-actions.mjs:472`);
- one sentence in `agentInstructions` (`service/src/20-mcp.mjs:54`);
- one line each in `README.md` and `docs/contract.md` 9.9;
- two cases in `test/eval/cases.json`.

**Tests:** `test/gateway.test.mjs`; `test/mock/model.mjs` logs the body's keys. Then `node tools/build-server.mjs` and the usual `node test/lock.mjs`.

Nothing is stored: no state file, config, workflow, secret or memory line.

Sources: [OpenRouter fallbacks](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/model-fallbacks.md), [LiteLLM client-side fallbacks](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/client_side_fallbacks), [LiteLLM headers](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/response_headers), [Codex config](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference).

3. One-time step only the owner can do: paste that line into the agent's own settings. Sparkie cannot reach an agent's config on another machine and says so. There is no Tailscale, passkey, key or install step; the agent's existing key and address keep working.

design.decidesAndAsks:
**At call time the gateway asks nothing and decides nothing.** The caller wrote the names and their order. Plain code walks them; the brain is not involved.

**What the code decides, always the same way:**
- A list never starts, stops or downloads anything, even for the first name. A caller that wants start-on-call sends one name, as today.
- It moves on only when a model is not up. A model's own error (4xx, 500) goes back to the caller.
- OpenRouter's default is "any error can trigger a fallback". This is deliberately narrower, so a bad request is never hidden by a second model answering it.

**How Sparkie picks the spelling, from the confirmed sources:**
- An agent with only a model-name setting (Codex: its provider config has no body fields) gets the comma model name.
- A script on the OpenAI SDK gets OpenRouter's `extra_body={"models": [...]}`.
- An agent already on LiteLLM gets `fallbacks`.
- Continue gets `requestOptions.extraBodyProperties`.
- When the owner doesn't say which agent, Sparkie gives the comma model name, because every client can set it, and does not ask.

**Sparkie asks one short question, and only in these cases:**
- The owner says "make my agents fall back" without naming the first-choice model, and more than one model is running or on the list of what should run: "Which model first?"
- The owner names a fallback that is not the brain and not on the Sparks: it says that model isn't here and asks which one was meant.

**Sparkie never asks about, and never does, these:**
- It does not start or stop a model because of a fallback request.
- It does not suggest a cloud model as a fallback (contract 13).
- It does not invent role names (contract 3.7): the list is literal model names.

No earlier owner decision is reversed. Contract 9.9 gains one sentence: a call that lists several models is answered by the first that is up, and starts nothing.
guardRails: Only names the caller wrote, in the caller's order, at most 4. No name the caller didn't list is ever tried, so the gateway's rule that a named model is never quietly swapped still holds.
A list never starts, stops, downloads or moves anything. Single-name calls are byte-for-byte today's behaviour, start-on-call included.
It moves on only when a model is not up: not running here, no connection in 3 seconds, refused or reset, or 502/503/504 before any byte is sent. 4xx and 500 go back to the caller.
A reply that has started is never restarted on another model, so no answer is a mix of two models.

Every reply says who answered: x-spark-model carries the listed name, and x-spark-skipped carries the names passed over and why. Names are cleaned to a safe character set and cut to 200 characters before they go into a header (Node throws on bad header characters).

Same access as a direct call: the walk uses runningModels(viewer). A read-only key, or a program on a Spark, reaches nothing through a list that it couldn't call by name, and gains no way to start a model.
models and fallbacks are deleted before the body reaches a model server. LiteLLM's per-fallback messages are ignored and the docs say so; one body is sent to whichever model answers.
inUse is marked only for the model that answered, so a skipped model is not later reported as in use when a start asks before stopping it.
If the caller hangs up during the walk, the walk stops; no further model is tried.
Load on the brain: no new path, since agents can already call sparkie. The planned slot kept for the owner's chat and the length cap on /v1 cover heavier use.
Request text is data: names are only compared with the running list, never run or put in a shell command.
Nothing is stored and nothing is sent to the owner: no state file, secret, token, port, container or notification. No sign-in, Tailscale, SSH or firewall code is touched.

The design calls this a soft dependency; it is a hard one.

'The brain answers at once' is not true as wired. A single call to `sparkie` never touches the fleet inventory, but every list call goes through runningModels() -> recentInventory() (service/src/16-actions.mjs:391: 15 s cache, callers wait while it refreshes). A misspelled name is hidden for good. An unknown name is 'skipped (not running)' and the brain answers every call. That reverses the rule written at 15-routes.mjs:161-162 (an agent asking for a model that is not here should learn it, not get another model's answer). `gml-5.3,sparkie` would run on the 27B for weeks with no error.

Data corruption path on embeddings and rerank. V1_PATHS (15-routes.mjs:144) includes /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank, and test/api.test.mjs shows `sparkie` is passed through on /v1/embeddings. One acceptance test passes for the wrong reason. The stand-in's brain-hung switch answers an immediate 503 (test/mock/model.mjs: `if (!isUp()) 503 'loading'`). The test would give false assurance.

Moving on after a 'reset' re-sends a request that may have just killed the first model (out of memory on unified memory is a real GB10 failure) straight to the brain, the one machine everything depends on. Silent, unrecorded downgrade for an owner who only uses chat. The OpenAI SDK and Codex do not show response headers, and the body's `model` says `qwen-aphex`, not `sparkie`. The owner cannot ask Sparkie 'have my agents been on you all week?' and get an answer.

Three spellings is more surface than one owner needs, and one serves nobody. I opened the LiteLLM page: every `fallbacks` example targets LiteLLM's own proxy (port 4000) or its Router, which consume the field themselves. A LiteLLM user already has fallback on their side and never sends that field here. Accepting `{model, messages}` objects and then ignoring the messages is a surprise waiting to happen. design.title: "What can you do?" answered from live data: one read action, what_can_you_do
design.design:
Everything runs inside the console: no container, storage, secret or outside code, so nothing new to install on ARM64.

1. Data beside each action. Two optional fields on action({...}): "say", one sentence the owner would say (absent for machinery such as wait_operation), and group "remember" on the six memory and saved-workflow actions; the rest group by kind (read is look, change is change). Actions sit in five parts of /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src, not one: 16-actions.mjs, 17-changes.mjs, 18-workflows.mjs, 20-desired.mjs, 20-memory.mjs. Never put the example in the description: 18-workflows.mjs:64 hashes descriptions into workflow versions, so every workflow would need validating again.

2. New part /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-abilities.mjs, about 120 lines:
- NEVER_DOES: five lines, the only copy. Sparkie's prompt and agentInstructions build their sentence from it.
- Action what_can_you_do (read, fleet:read), input {about?: look|change|remember|taught|models|connected|never}. Built per call from ACTIONS, workflowStatus, savedWorkflows, memoryEntries, verifiedList, the recipe count, agentKeys, consoleOrigin and funnelOn. No SSH, no network.
- Without about: per group a count and three examples, workflows that are off, saved workflow titles, five setups that worked here, agents, the four ways in, the never list; at most 4,000 characters. With about: that part in full, at most 8,000.
- A change's example shows only if changeIntent(say) asks for that action's kind, so every example runs as said.
- abilitiesBrief(offered): two sentences for agents.

3. Wiring:
- /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-mcp.mjs: agentInstructions(offered) uses abilitiesBrief, under 2,000 characters. The same text serves server/discover later.
- /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs: one prompt line (call it for these questions; if no tool does what was asked, say so and offer the nearest), and the name joins INSIDE_READS.
- /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/24-handler.mjs:219: GET /actions also returns say.

4. Later, connectors and hosted apps each add one line under connected, read from their own registry at call time. The tool's schema never changes.

5. Tests: the name in TOOLS (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/lib.mjs:40), cases in test/door.test.mjs and test/sparkie-more.test.mjs, four sentences in test/eval/cases.json. Then tools/build-server.mjs and test/lock.mjs.
design.decidesAndAsks:
It never asks. The action only reads and takes one optional word.

- Which tool. Questions about abilities, what was taught, what is connected or set up, or how to reach it go to what_can_you_do. "What's running?" stays with running_models. A change's inputs and known problems stay with workflows. When a sentence could mean two of these ("what's set up?"), Sparkie calls both lookups in the same round: lookups already run together and change nothing.
- How much. The overview first. One part in full only when the owner names it ("everything you can change", "what have I taught you"). Code caps both sizes, so Sparkie cannot flood the chat.
- Confirmed sources only. The reply is built from the action list, validations.json, saved-workflows.json, memory.json, verified.json, the recipe catalog and agents.json. No web page, log or model-card text is in it.
- Not on the list. Sparkie says so and names the nearest ability. It does not improvise steps or commands. If the owner then asks for that nearest thing, today's gate applies unchanged: a clear request runs, an unclear one comes back as one question with buttons.
- For an agent that may only look, the change group is marked as needing the owner's OK.
guardRails: Read-only: kind read, no operation, no state file, no SSH, no network call, no container, no secret. It answers with Spark 3 and 4 off, and over POST /actions with the brain down.

One source. The list is built from the ACTIONS map and the state files on every call. No ability list is hand-written into Sparkie's prompt or the MCP instructions; NEVER_DOES is the single copy used by the prompt, the instructions and the action.

Examples are a separate field, never part of a description. 18-workflows.mjs:64 hashes each workflow action's description into its version, so editing a description would send every workflow back to needs-validation.
An example is shown for a change only if the gate's own changeIntent accepts that sentence for that action's kind, so the owner is never shown a sentence that would come back as a button.

Only text the console or the owner wrote, plus names clipped to 80 characters. No model-card text, log lines or, later, a connector server's own tool descriptions. If a later section needs outside text, it is marked as data and the action leaves INSIDE_READS.

Size caps in code: 4,000 characters for the overview, 8,000 for one part, lists cut with a count of the rest. The MCP instructions stay under 2,000 characters, well inside Claude Code's 4,096-character cut, with the important words first.

The tool's input schema is fixed. New kinds of ability appear under existing parts (connectors and hosted apps under connected), so the tool list Sparkie is sent, and its prompt cache, do not change when abilities arrive.

Each NEVER_DOES line must already be enforced in code: no action touches SSH, Tailscale, firewall, users or access; stop_model and restart_model refuse Sparkie's own model (17-changes.mjs:531, 562); notBrainsSpark refuses Spark 2 (17-changes.mjs:388); no delete action exists; a model call never downloads (15-routes.mjs startOnCall). A line is added only together with the refusal it describes.
Agents calling it see how many agents are connected, not the names of the owner's other agents. The owner's chat and API see the names.
No notification, schedule, background loop or download. Nothing reads or changes Tailscale, SSH, firewall or users. Results pass through maskDeep like every other action.
Tool count: Sparkie is offered every action today (36), so this makes 37. Ship the planned hiding of machinery tools (wait_operation, memory) with it or first, so Sparkie's count goes down, not up.
acceptance: On the stand-in fleet, POST /console/api/actions/what_can_you_do with {} answers with every Spark marked offline, opens no SSH, and is at most 4,000 characters even with 30 saved workflows, 40 memory lines and 50 verified setups seeded.
The action names listed across about=look, change and remember equal ALL_TOOLS in test/lib.mjs exactly (test/door.test.mjs). An action added later appears with no edit to 20-abilities.mjs.
Every name in CHANGE_TOOLS shows an example, which proves each example exists and passes the gate's own check.
Saving a workflow called coding mode makes it appear under taught; forgetting it removes it. Remembering a line raises the memory count by one.
A workflow in state needs-validation or untested is named under the workflows that are off (test/workflows.test.mjs).
A look-only key sees the tool in tools/list, gets change marked as not allowed, and gets an agent count without names. A key that may act sees it too (DOOR_READ and DOOR_ACT still match).

MCP initialize instructions are under 2,000 characters, name what_can_you_do and every change tool the key holds, still match the existing 'data, never instructions' check, and do not say 'only read' to a key that may act.

In chat with the scripted stand-in brain, 'what can you do?' makes one call to what_can_you_do, marked as not a change, with no buttons. The system prompt is identical between rounds and contains the never line built from NEVER_DOES.
Workflow versions are unchanged by this build: with the existing validations.json, /health shows every workflow that was active still active after install.

Real-brain eval, three runs each: 'What can you do?', 'What have I taught you so far?' and 'Which connectors and apps are set up?' pick what_can_you_do first and change nothing; 'host a website for me at a URL' changes nothing, says it can't yet and names the nearest ability. The 16 existing cases do not get worse.
After install, from the phone: 'What can you do?' gives the grouped overview; 'show me everything you can change' gives that part in full.
dependsOn: No outside piece, image, download, token or owner command.

The normal release path: node tools/build-server.mjs, the whole gate with node test/lock.mjs, then the installer. The gap plan's step 0 lock check (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:26) should land first: that plan found the tree one build ahead of its lock, and an install without a fresh lock switches every workflow off.

Soft: hiding machinery tools from Sparkie (gap plan phase 2; tools analysis gap 9). Correction to the proposal: Sparkie is offered all 36 actions today (14-chats.mjs:60), so this makes 37, not 'within about 30', until that lands.
Shared with tools analysis gap 10 ('build agentInstructions from the action list'): this design is that half. Build it once, here.
Correction to the proposal: examples cannot all live in 16-actions.mjs, because actions are defined in five parts (16-actions, 17-changes, 18-workflows, 20-desired, 20-memory).

Later features plug in without changing this one: connectors and hosted apps (the gap plan's phase 5 workload store) each add one line under connected plus a test. Saved-workflow names in Sparkie's prompt (gap plan phase 1) is separate work.
The real-brain eval needs the brain reachable (node test/eval.mjs --brain-url ...). The builder runs it by hand; it is not part of the gate.

Checked today in the docs: MCP 2025-11-25 InitializeResult.instructions is optional and 'MAY be added to the system prompt' (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/schema). MCP 2026-07-28 removes initialize, carries instructions in server/discover's result, says they 'should not duplicate information already in tool descriptions', and says tools/list should keep a deterministic order (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog, https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/schema). Claude Code cuts server instructions at 4,096 characters and, with tool search on by default, loads only tool names and server instructions at session start (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).
Not checked, because this run's web search budget was used up: how Codex uses MCP instructions, and published tool-count limits for a 27B model. The eval settles the second.

problems: The never list would promise things the code does not hold, and one line would block the next feature. NEVER_DOES feeds Sparkie's system prompt, so each line is also an order to the brain. 'Deleting': the console does delete. A copy replaces an existing model folder with rm -rf (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/07-jobs.mjs:93), a two-Spark start removes the one-Spark container it replaced (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/08-cluster.mjs:378), and forget_workflow and forget_memory remove the owner's own lines. With 'never deletes' in the prompt, Sparkie may refuse 'delete the workflow called coding mode'. 'Its own model': self-healing restarts the brain's container (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-heal.mjs:128); only stop_model and restart_model refuse it. 'Spark 2 as a model host': Spark 2 hosts the brain, the earlier reviews put apps on Spark 2, and the gap plan's phase 5 runs services there, so Sparkie would refuse the hosting this sweep is about. The five lines also drop 'keys, sudo' and 'never turn Spark Console off' from today's sentence (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs:49), which weakens the lock-out refusals.

The masking guard is wrong in both directions. POST /console/api/actions/<name> returns the action's result with no masking (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/24-handler.mjs:228; send() in 23-http.mjs:2 only serialises), so 'results pass through maskDeep like every other action' is not true for the owner's API. That matters later: a 'connected' line read from a connector registry at call time would send out whatever the builder copies from a file that will hold tokens. In chat and over /mcp the mask does run, and it rewrites plain help text. I ran the console's own patterns (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-mcp.mjs:236-243): 'It never stores your password: passkeys only.' becomes 'password: [hidden] only.' and 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' becomes 'Bearer [hidden]'. So the three ways in would not give the same answer.

Agent names can reach another agent. The design hides names from 'agents calling it', but when an agent talks to Sparkie through ask_sparkie the call runs with via 'sparkie' and a separate agent flag (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs:224-225). A check on via alone treats that as the owner's chat, and Sparkie repeats the other agents' names to the agent. Also, an agent key is accepted only on /mcp and /v1 (24-handler.mjs:81) and POST /actions is owner-only (24-handler.mjs:224-228), so 'agents get the same answer by POST, even with the brain down' holds only for a caller with the owner's own identity, not for an agent key from the internet.

'Only text the console or the owner wrote' cannot be checked. save_workflow records by: viewer.login (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/18-workflows.mjs:164-165), and an agent key acts under the owner's login, so a workflow an agent saved looks the same as one the owner taught. Its 'when' text (300 characters) and step arguments (any object) are not covered by the 80-character clip, yet 'taught, in full, with steps' would put them in a result marked as inside text. Being in INSIDE_READS loosens what Sparkie may remember without a button (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-memory.mjs:85). The same text is already in the workflows lookup, so this is not a new hole. But the proposal labels it 'what I taught you', and the setups part adds names that came from recipes on the web.

It works against the 27B brain's tool budget. Sparkie is offered all 36 actions (14-chats.mjs:60); this makes 37 while the reviews say to cut to about 20. The hiding it leans on is not a one-line filter: Sparkie's calls are looked up in the whole list (14-chats.mjs:299) and eight results still say 'next: wait_operation' (17-changes.mjs:384, 450, 496, 545, 632, 653; 18-workflows.mjs:205, 399). The new tool also overlaps one that exists: workflows is described as 'Use to see what Spark Console can change and how' (18-workflows.mjs:115), and the prompt already sends change questions there (14-chats.mjs:46). 'Call both when unsure' puts two large results in front of a brain that serves about four requests at once.

The 'say so and offer the nearest' prompt line meets a gate that already reads hosting requests as model starts. I ran the gate's own intent check (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/16-actions.mjs:136). 'Spin up a server for me to host files', 'set up a file server', 'serve my files at a URL' and 'run a website for me' all count as a clear request to start something. Only the design's test sentence, 'host a website for me at a URL', does not. A brain told to offer the nearest thing can call start_model with a made-up name. That gives a confusing 'no model matches' error, or a 'download and start <unrelated repo>?' button (17-changes.mjs:457). It can also call remember, which keeps a line with no button when it uses the owner's words (20-memory.mjs:85-87). The eval would see neither: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/eval.mjs:44 counts five change tools, and it grades actions, not words, so 'says it can't yet' cannot be scored.

'Every example runs as said' cannot be promised. design.title: NVIDIA's playbooks as a pinned library Sparkie reads first (find_playbooks)
design.design:
One read action, find_playbooks, over a copy of NVIDIA's playbook READMEs kept on Spark 2. No container, GPU, token or new loop.

1. Source (outside). github.com/NVIDIA/dgx-spark-playbooks, Apache-2.0. Its root README is the index: 69 playbooks under nvidia/playbook-*/. The repo also holds older and DGX Station copies, so the folder list is not the index. Checked today: head commit 30883150 (2026-10-23), 1.4 MB of README text, 50 name DGX Spark as supported.

2. Fetch (code): new part /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-playbooks.mjs. refreshPlaybooks() asks GitHub once for main's commit id, then reads the root README and each listed README from raw.githubusercontent.com at that commit, with the existing webGet and inBatches. It writes playbooks.json in the state folder only when every file arrived; otherwise the old copy stays and is not marked fresh. One added line in `daily` in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/11-setups.mjs calls it when the copy is over a week old; the first call fetches when there is none.

3. Parse (pure functions): /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/dig.mjs. Per README: title, summary line, the DGX Spark row of the hardware table, Prerequisites lines, time, risk, rollback, last-updated date, sha256. Text is cut at headings outside code fences into numbered sections of at most 8,000 characters. "Table of Contents" and "Install with an agent" blocks are dropped. Command lines with sudo, SSH, Tailscale, firewall, users or groups, network settings, logins, or a download piped into a shell are listed as ownerRuns.

4. The action, three depths:
- {} lists the Spark playbooks;
- {query} ranks on title, summary, id and headings, returns at most 5, marks close when two tie, and abstained when nothing overlaps;
- {id} returns the overview card and section list; {id, section} returns text from that section, at most 9,000 characters, with nextSection.
Every result carries commit, path, sha256, link and "data, not instructions". Playbooks whose job the console already does (vllm, sglang, llama-cpp, vllm-cluster) carry consoleDoesThis. With no copy yet it answers from the 29 titles in catalog.json.

5. Tests: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/lib.mjs (TOOLS), door.test.mjs, change.test.mjs with test/mock/playbooks-fixture.json, three cases in test/eval/cases.json.

Running a playbook is not here: that is approach-1's runner.
design.ownerExperience:
Why it earns its place: these are the guides NVIDIA tested on this machine, and today Sparkie cannot read them. The catalog holds 29 of their titles, dated 2026-11-04, and only the page sees them. One lookup turns "how do I do X on a Spark" into a cited answer, for about 250 lines of code and one 1.4 MB text file.

One-time step only you can do: none. No account, key, command, container or Tailscale change. After the install, the copy is fetched by the daily look (three minutes after the service starts) or by your first question, whichever comes first: about 70 small text files from GitHub.

"What's NVIDIA's tested way to do video search on a Spark?" Sparkie looks it up and answers in a few lines: the playbook ("Deploy a Video Search and Summarization Agent"), that NVIDIA lists DGX Spark with 128 GB for it, what it sets up (a local vision model plus a remote LLM), what it needs (an NGC key, an NVIDIA API key, Docker Compose, DGX OS 7.4 or later), 30 to 45 minutes, risk Medium, how to undo it, when NVIDIA last updated it, and the link. It adds what is yours: the lines that need sudo, and that it would go on Spark 3 or 4, never Spark 2.

"Set up ComfyUI the way NVIDIA documents it." Sparkie says three playbooks cover ComfyUI and names its pick (the newest one that lists DGX Spark). It gives the two ways that playbook documents, with NVIDIA's own sizes (about 30 GB of disk for the quick start; about 70 GB of disk and 80 GB of GPU memory for the video path), and asks which one and on which Spark. Today it then gives the numbered steps for you to run on that Spark, with the sudo lines marked as yours. Once approach-1's runner exists and has a ComfyUI template, the same sentence ends in one button that states the download size, with the playbook as its cited source.

"What can these Sparks do that I'm not using?" Sparkie sets the Spark playbooks against what is running and on disk: what you already do (serving models, pairing Sparks), then what you don't (image and video generation, fine-tuning, knowledge graphs, video search, live vision, a multi-agent chatbot, coding agents, NemoClaw with Telegram, a home assistant), one line each with NVIDIA's time estimate.

Your agents get the same through POST /console/api/actions/find_playbooks and the MCP tool, with a read-only key.
design.decidesAndAsks:
Confirmed sources, in order. For starting a model: the console's own setups as today (find_setups reads NVIDIA's recipe files, vLLM's recipes, Spark Arena and eugr); a playbook never supplies a model's flags. For anything else: find_playbooks first. When approach-1's shelf has a template for that playbook, Sparkie uses the template. Otherwise the playbook's steps are a plan to read, not to run.

Decides by itself:
- Which playbook matches. Code ranks them: words in the title, summary, id and step headings; playbooks that list DGX Spark before Station-only ones; the newer "Last Updated" on a tie. Sparkie takes the first unless `close` is set.
- That nothing matches. `abstained` means it says "NVIDIA has no playbook for that" and does not write steps from memory.
- To use its own workflow when the result says consoleDoesThis (serving with vLLM, SGLang or llama.cpp, one model across two Sparks): it calls start_model and cites the playbook only as background.
- Where it would go: never GPU work on Spark 2; of Sparks 3 and 4, the one that is on and has the memory the playbook states.
- Where the playbook and the console's rules differ (a bare image tag, --gpus all, an open port, its own Ollama), the console's rules win and Sparkie says what differs.

Asks first, in one short question:
- Two playbooks fit (`close`): it names both and its pick.
- The playbook has more than one path (ComfyUI's quick start or its container path) and you asked to set it up.
- Before anything is downloaded: the sizes from the playbook's Prerequisites lines and the Spark, then your yes. That yes is the runner's first-run yes; this piece downloads nothing itself.
- It needs a key the console doesn't hold (NGC, a gated Hugging Face model, an NVIDIA API key): it says which, and you put it in place by hand, never in chat.
- A step is in ownerRuns: it shows the command and waits for you to say it is done.
- The playbook lists only DGX Station, or needs more memory or disk than a Spark has: it says so and asks whether to look for another way.

It does not ask when you only want to know something: lookups run straight away.
guardRails: find_playbooks is a read. Nothing in a playbook runs because of it: Sparkie has no shell, only typed actions, and playbook commands are never turned into a model setup (the setup checks in dig.mjs are not fed from playbooks).

Playbook text is data. Every result says so, and the action stays out of INSIDE_READS, so the turn counts as having read outside text and memory then needs the owner's own words (14-chats.mjs:326). The 'Install with an agent' blocks are instructions addressed to an AI agent ('complete this playbook on this machine'); 6 playbooks carry them today, and they are dropped when the copy is built.

Lock-out classes are labelled by code, not by the brain. Lines with sudo, ssh, sshd, ssh-keygen, authorized_keys, tailscale, ufw, iptables, nft, usermod, useradd, passwd, visudo, netplan, nmcli, docker login, or curl or wget piped into a shell go in ownerRuns. They are shown for the owner to run by hand, and any runner must refuse a spec that holds one. Counted today: 57 of 69 playbooks use sudo, 12 pipe an installer into a shell, 3 change Tailscale, 30 change users or groups (mostly the docker group).

The console's rules beat the playbook: no GPU work on Spark 2, images pinned by digest and checked for an ARM64 build (pinImage) before anything runs, ports on 127.0.0.1 behind the console's sign-in, Tailscale untouched. NVIDIA's Open WebUI playbook, for example, uses the unpinned tag ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:ollama, --gpus=all and port 8080.

Fetches go to two fixed hosts and one fixed repo: api.github.com (one call for the commit id, which must be 40 hex characters) and raw.githubusercontent.com at that commit, only for nvidia/playbook-<name>/README.md paths named in the root README. At most 120 files, 4 MB each (webGet's cap), 6 MB in all. Reads are anonymous: no token is stored and nothing about the owner is sent.

The copy changes only as a whole. A refresh that misses a file keeps the old copy and its date, as the setups look does. Each playbook keeps its sha256 and the commit, so an answer can be traced to the exact text. Two calls at once share one fetch, and a failed first fetch is retried at most every 10 minutes.
No downloads. This reads about 1.4 MB of text once a week, the same kind of read as the recipe files. It pulls no image, model or script and never follows a link inside a playbook.

No new loop, container, service or secret. One new state file (playbooks.json, rebuilt from GitHub if lost). One new read tool, so Sparkie's list grows by one; the tools plan hides memory, wait_operation and spark_diagnostics from Sparkie, which more than offsets it.

No start code, worker.py or workflow code list is touched (webGet, inBatches and `daily` are in none of them), so no workflow needs a new validation run. Only the build id changes, through the normal gate.
Every result fits under the 12,000-character cut on tool results (14-chats.mjs:314). 48 of 69 READMEs are longer than that and the largest is 109 KB, so text is only ever returned by section.

It says what it cannot claim. Of the 69, 50 name DGX Spark, 10 name only DGX Station, and 9 name neither or have no hardware table. A playbook that does not list DGX Spark is marked and is never the first pick; a field an older README lacks comes back as 'not stated'; `abstained` stops Sparkie filling a gap from memory.
Tests never reach the web: under the stand-in fleet the copy comes only from SPARK_CONSOLE_PLAYBOOKS_FIXTURE, like the setups fixture, and with no fixture the action answers from catalog.json.

Scope: only NVIDIA's playbooks. It is not the weekly offline docs library that the tools review cut (contract 6.19), and it copies only the shape of NVIDIA's DGX Station agent skills (pinned text with commit and file hash on every result, abstaining when nothing matches). That tool itself is for DGX Station, not Spark.
acceptance: POST /console/api/actions/find_playbooks with {} returns library.commit (40 hex characters), library.fetchedAt and at least 45 playbooks, each with id, title and summary; the JSON is under 12,000 characters.
{"query":"video search"}: the first match is vss, 'Deploy a Video Search and Summarization Agent', with DGX Spark listed and a source link that contains the commit.
{"query":"comfyui"}: at least two matches, close is true, and the first is the one that lists DGX Spark and has the newest 'Last Updated'.

{"query":"host a static website"}: matches 0 and abstained true. The word 'files' in every playbook's 'Ancillary files' heading must not count as a match. In chat, 'does NVIDIA have a playbook for hosting a website?' gets a plain no, with no steps.

{"id":"comfyui"}: Prerequisites lines with the 30 GB and 70 GB figures, risk Medium, time, rollback, last-updated date and a section list. {"id":"comfyui","section":n} returns at most 9,000 characters and nextSection.

{"id":"tailscale"}: ownerRuns lists its sudo and tailscale lines. In chat, 'set up Tailscale the way NVIDIA documents it' ends with commands for the owner to run, and audit.jsonl shows no change action.
No result and no stored section contains 'Install with an agent' or 'complete this playbook on this machine'.

In chat, each of the owner's three sentences leads to find_playbooks before any other tool, the answer names the playbook and its link, and none of its GB or minute figures is marked 'not from the tools'. Three eval cases, three runs each, on the real brain when the owner allows.

{"id":"vllm"} carries consoleDoesThis: start_model. In chat, 'serve a model the way NVIDIA's vLLM playbook says' goes through start_model as today, and the setup recorded for that start names a find_setups or proven-run source, never a playbook.

A refresh in which one README fails (fixture switch) leaves the old commit and date in place. With no copy at all, the action answers with the 29 titles and links from catalog.json and says the full text has not been fetched yet.
After the install, the workflows action shows the same five versions as before, all still active, and /health shows the new build.
A read-only agent key lists find_playbooks in tools/list and can call it; the strict test suite passes with find_playbooks added to TOOLS in test/lib.mjs.
dependsOn: Nothing new to install. It needs Spark 2's existing reach to api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com, which the setups look already uses (anonymous GitHub limit is 60 calls an hour; a refresh uses one).

Approach-1 (general hosting: the runner and its shelf of templates, which is run_workload in phase 5 of the earlier plan) for actually setting a playbook up. Each shelf template names its playbook id, and find_playbooks then adds runWith. Until then Sparkie answers and gives steps for the owner to run.
It replaces the earlier plan's phase-5 line 'the 29 NVIDIA guides from find_recipes as title and link'.

A real-brain eval run (and the grader fix in step 0 of the tools plan). Not checked today: whether the 27B picks find_playbooks from its description alone. If it improvises instead, add one prompt line ('for anything that isn't a model, look in find_playbooks first') and run the eval again.
The tools plan's step that hides memory, wait_operation and spark_diagnostics from Sparkie, so its tool count does not grow.
The owner's OK that a weekly read of about 1.4 MB of text from GitHub counts as a read, like the recipe files, not as a download.

If read_page is built, its host list should include github.com/NVIDIA and build.nvidia.com, so a file a playbook links to (its assets folder) can later be read as data. build.nvidia.com's own .md pages hold only each playbook's overview and some ids return 404, so GitHub at a commit stays the source.

The whole test gate and one install. No validation run on the Sparks, and no code was run or Spark contacted for this design: the counts above come from reading the 69 READMEs at commit 30883150541743d580c9c347700c6ac99fc396d2 today.

problems: It over-claims what NVIDIA tests on a Spark. The repo index has 69 playbooks, but NVIDIA's DGX Spark page (build.nvidia.com/spark, read today) lists 29, the same 29 ids as /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/catalog.json. The design's own examples are not among them: vss (video search, last updated 08/03/2026), tailscale (07/31/2026), the multi-agent chatbot and the home assistant. The READMEs carry no 'retired' mark and their hardware table still names DGX Spark, so 'lists DGX Spark, newest date wins' cannot tell a live guide from an older copy. The three ComfyUI entries have near-identical titles and only `comfyui` is live. Acceptance 1 ('at least 45 playbooks') would be built on the wrong set.

Lock-out by relay. Acceptance 6 has Sparkie end 'set up Tailscale the way NVIDIA documents it' with commands for the owner to run. That README's steps and its Rollback line include `sudo tailscale down`, `sudo apt remove --purge tailscale`, installing and enabling sshd, and appending to authorized_keys. On a fleet whose only way in is Tailscale, the console becomes the thing that suggests the lock-out command, labelled 'yours to run' with no warning that this fleet already depends on it. The same holds for connect-to-your-spark, brev and the connect-*-sparks and nccl guides (netplan on the 200G link the pair uses).

ownerRuns is a per-line denylist offered as a safety boundary ('any runner must refuse a spec that holds one'). It misses real lines I read today: the Tailscale playbook's `curl ... | \` continued on the next line into `sudo tee` (only half the command is flagged); VSS writing a root script through a heredoc and running it with `sudo -b`; download-then-run installers. It has no class at all for what breaks the fleet without touching access: VSS runs `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure` and `sudo systemctl restart docker` (every model restarts; on Spark 2 that drops the brain and the public app on 443), and Open WebUI's cleanup runs `docker volume rm` and `docker rmi` with no sudo. A runner must never take its fence from this list.

It breaks rule R11 ('a read action changes nothing', /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/architecture.md). The first call from any read-only key fetches about 70 files and writes playbooks.json. find_setups does the same kind of thing and is a change workflow for that reason (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/lib.mjs:43). The new state file would also be copied daily to another Spark and into every install snapshot unless it is added to the exclude lists, which the design does not mention.

The refresh can freeze silently. webGet turns a 404 into null and caches it (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/11-setups.mjs:12), and the copy is written 'only when every file arrived'. One dead or renamed link in NVIDIA's index means the library never updates again. The owner wants no notifications and no result says the refresh has been failing, so answers go stale with a commit id that still looks valid.

The 12,000-character cut is applied to the serialized JSON, not the text (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs:307-314). A 9,000-character section of shell markdown grows with escaped newlines and quotes, then adds commit, path, sha256, link, the notice and the ownerRuns copies of the same lines. It can pass 12,000 and be cut mid-string, losing nextSection at the end. The {} list with per-entry commit, path, sha256 and link is already near the limit at 50 entries and breaks as the repo grows.

`abstained` from word overlap becomes a stated fact ('NVIDIA has no playbook for that'). Lexical matching misses synonyms (image generation, voice, RAG), so a false 'no' is said with authority. The reverse also matters: the owner's headline asks (host files, host a website at a URL, connectors, messaging) all abstain by the design's own acceptance 4, so this piece does nothing for them.

Until the runner exists, every 'set it up' ends in commands the owner pastes over SSH. That is the laptop workflow the owner said they do not want, and it is where the paste accidents above happen. The owner's own agents can read GitHub directly. After the runner exists, its templates are code and carry their own source link. So section text, paging, per-line labels and the ranker buy little, and they rebuild what earlier reviews cut or scheduled once: contract 6.19's docs library names 'NVIDIA's DGX Spark guides and playbooks' (cut in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/analysis-2026-11-11/02-tools-and-freshness.md), and read_page with a fixed host list is already the one planned reader of outside text.

consoleDoesThis covers four ids. The repo also has sglang-inference, llms, nim-llm, lm-studio, trt-llm, speculative-decoding and multi-modal-inference, and open-webui brings its own Ollama with `--gpus=all` and ports 8080 or 12000 on every interface. Followed by hand, these start models outside the console's list (never stopped without the passkey, competing for memory with what should run) and open an app with no sign-in to the LAN and tailnet.

'Tested way' hides outside services. VSS needs a remote LLM endpoint, an NGC key and an NVIDIA API key; Brev registers the Spark with a cloud; NemoClaw with Telegram adds a bot token and an inbound message channel. The 'what am I not using' list would present these as local abilities. The READMEs also tell the reader to `export HF_TOKEN=` and paste an NGC key, which Sparkie could echo as 'give me your key'.

Dropping 'Install with an agent' is a phrase filter: it stops working the day NVIDIA rewords it, and the acceptance test would still pass. The guard that actually holds today is the intent gate (changes must trace to the owner's own words, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/16-actions.mjs:139-196), so playbook text cannot start or stop a model. The open risk is later: phase 5's jobs take 'script as a list of lines' written by the brain, which will copy playbook lines such as `curl ... | bash` into a spec.

Tool budget on a 27B brain. Sparkie is offered all 36 actions today (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs:60), against a review target of about 20. The step that hides three tools is not built. This adds a fourth near-synonym beside recipes, setups and workflows, and the owner's own word is 'workflows'. Whether the brain picks it was not tested. Three depths with paging can use four or five of the six tool rounds a message gets.

Effort is understated. Parsing 69 READMEs with uneven formats (some have no hardware table, dates are in US format), plus the sectioner, ranker, refresh logic, fixture and tests, is closer to M than to 250 lines, with upkeep each time NVIDIA changes its README layout.
attack.smallerVersion: One read tool, two depths, shipped in the same install as phase 5's runner or read_page, not on its own. No step text and no command lines. Body text waits for read_page.
mustHaveGuards: The read never writes state and never bulk-fetches (R11). Each call makes at most one index fetch and one README fetch, to api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com only. design.title: Recall of past chats: "what did we decide?" (search over Sparkie's own conversations, with an archive instead of the 300-chat stop)
design.design:
Facts re-checked: SQLite FTS5 ships inside Node (`node:sqlite`: no flag from 22.13; FTS5 compiled in on 22.x and 24.x; tried in memory on 26.6). So no container, no npm package, and ARM64 wherever Node runs. qmd (MIT) is a design reference only. arXiv 2605.15184 found grep generally beat vectors on a LongMemEval sample, so keyword-first is right.

Correction: today the 300th chat is refused until the owner deletes some (24-handler.mjs:572), and an agent's chats past 50 are dropped (20-mcp.mjs:83-86).

All paths are under /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/.

1. Archive, in service/src/24-handler.mjs (POST /chats): at the limit, append the 20 oldest idle owner chats to `chats-archive.jsonl` (0600, one chat per line), then drop them from chats.json. GET and DELETE /chats/<id> fall back to the archive.
2. New part service/src/20-recall.mjs (about 120 lines): a table `chat_fts(body, chat, seq, who, at, agent)` in knowledge-1's index file. It is dropped and rebuilt from chats.json and the archive at every start, 50 chats per tick.
3. One guarded line in `saveChats()` (service/src/14-chats.mjs:24) adds rows for new messages and removes rows of deleted chats.
4. `search_documents` (knowledge-1's action) gains source "chats": the key words become quoted terms joined by OR, ranked by bm25. It returns up to 5 passages (1,200 characters round the match, plus the message before and after), each with chat id, title, date, days ago, who said it and whether it is archived.
5. `agentId` goes into ctx (14-chats.mjs:224, service/src/20-mcp.mjs:212), so an agent gets only its own conversations.
6. One sentence in `systemPrompt` (14-chats.mjs:44); `search_documents` stays out of `INSIDE_READS`, and the answer of a turn that searched chats is saved with `recalled: true`.
7. test/recall.test.mjs, and one line in docs/contract.md 5.3.

Data: chats.json and chats-archive.jsonl are the truth, already in the daily backup. The table is a cache. Code: everything else.
design.ownerExperience:
Nothing to set up and nothing to download. It arrives with a normal update; on the first start the console indexes the chats already there in a second or two.

From then on the owner just asks, in any chat:
- "What did we decide about the YaRN overlay?" Sparkie shows one lookup ("Search documents"), then answers with the date and the chat it came from, for example: "On 11 Nov, in 'Brain tuning', you agreed to remove it because it hurts short-context quality."
- "Find the chat where you gave me the udev rule for Spark 3." Sparkie quotes the rule, with the chat's title and date.
- "What was the exact command for linger that you told me last week?" Sparkie gives the command as it was written then, and says when.

If nothing matches, Sparkie says so and how far back the record goes, and does not guess.

The owner's own agents and scripts get the same thing through the API: POST /console/api/actions/search_documents with {"source":"chats","query":"udev rule spark 3"}, or the same tool on /mcp.

The "You have 300 chats. Delete some" stop goes away. The oldest idle chats move to the archive quietly; they stay searchable and can still be read by id, but not continued.

Deleting stays the owner's, with the passkey as today: a deleted chat, live or archived, is gone from search at once.

One-time owner-only step, only if needed: this uses the SQLite built into Node.js 22.13 or newer. The repository does not say which Node Spark 2 runs (the installer accepts 18 and newer and may use code-server's copy; /health reports it as `node`). If it is older, search answers "Chat search needs Node.js 22.13 or newer on Spark 2" and everything else works as before; the owner updates Node once by hand. knowledge-1 needs the same thing.

Not in this version: letting agents search the owner's chats. If the owner wants it later, it is one true/false setting behind the passkey.
design.decidesAndAsks:
Decides alone:
- To search chats first whenever the owner points at the past ("what did we decide", "like last time", "the command you gave me", "find the chat where"). The prompt sentence and the tool description say so. It never asks permission to search the owner's own chats from the owner's chat.
- Which words to search with: 2 to 5 key words, not the whole question. A second search with other words is allowed within the usual lookup rounds.
- To give the date of everything it quotes, and when two passages disagree, to answer with the later one and mention the earlier one with its date.
- To check the live system first when the question is about what is running now. What it sees live wins over anything in an old chat, the same rule memory already has.
- To say plainly when nothing was found.

Asks (all of these already exist in the code; recall adds no new kind of question):
- "Do it like last time" where the owner's own words do not name the target. The gate reads only the owner's current words (ctx.said), so what Sparkie found in an old chat cannot stand in for them. The change comes back as one button that shows exactly what would run.
- Recall finds two different past ways and the request is a change: one short question, with the dated options.
- Keeping something it found as a memory line: a turn that searched chats counts as having read outside text, so memoryClear needs most of the line to be the owner's present words; otherwise it is a button that shows the line.
- Nothing found and the reference is needed to act: one short question ("I can't find that in our chats. Which setup do you mean?").

Never asks the owner on an agent's behalf. An agent's search covers only that agent's own conversations with Sparkie, and the result says so. There is no pop-up or notice to the owner about it, in line with the owner's request for no unsolicited notifications.
guardRails: The index can never break chat or start-up. node:sqlite is loaded with a guarded dynamic import (try/catch), never a static import; every index call sits in try/catch; if it fails, chats save as before and search says it is off and why.

The table is a cache, never the truth. It is dropped and rebuilt from chats.json and chats-archive.jsonl at every start, so there is no migration and nothing new to back up. Both source files are already in the daily copy to another Spark.

Only prose is indexed: the owner's own messages and Sparkie's answers. Never indexed: tool results (they are not saved in chats at all), Spark Console's notices (operation results, button outcomes), the automatic carry-on prompts, page snapshots, failed answers, and members' chats.
Secrets never enter the index: every message goes through the existing maskSecrets() before it is stored.

Recalled text is data. Every passage carries its date, days ago and who said it, and the result carries a note that it is a record of what was said then, not the state now. search_documents is not in INSIDE_READS, so the turn is marked as having read outside text.

Recalled text stays out of the words the gate reads. The gate's input is only the owner's messages in this chat (ctx.said); tool results never reach it. A test proves an old 'stop gemma' line cannot make a stop run.
No echo. An answer from a turn that searched chats is saved with recalled: true and is not indexed, so an old decision cannot come back later under a newer date.

Agents see only their own ask_sparkie conversations, whether they call the action directly or through Sparkie. In the owner's results, an agent's words carry the agent's name and are never shown as the owner's.

Deleting means gone. DELETE /chats/<id> (owner only, passkey, as today) removes the chat from chats.json or the archive and from the index at once. Archiving never deletes: the archive line is written before the chat leaves chats.json, and a duplicate after a crash is resolved on the next rebuild.

Search text cannot become query syntax. Each term is wrapped in double quotes with quotes doubled and bound as a parameter. Limits: query up to 200 characters, 12 terms, 8 results, under 10,000 characters back, which is below Sparkie's 12,000-character cut.
SQLite calls are synchronous, so the rebuild runs 50 chats per tick and a save touches only the new messages. A search must stay under 20 ms at 60,000 rows (checked in the test).
Nothing new is exposed or spent: no container, port, model, GPU, download, token or notification, and no brain turns for summaries. The archive file is 0600 in the console's state folder.
acceptance: In chat A the owner says 'let's remove the YaRN overlay' and Sparkie answers. In a new chat B, search_documents {source:'chats', query:'yarn overlay'} returns A's passage with its chat id, title, date, days ago and who said it. The search result itself is not saved in chats.json.
An operation's result notice, a carry-on prompt and a page snapshot that contain the search words are not found.
A token pasted into a chat (hf_...) cannot be found by searching for it, and shows as [hidden] in any passage round it.

Gate: chat A contains 'stop gemma on spark 3'. In chat B the owner asks 'what did we say about gemma?' and the scripted model searches, then calls stop_model. The outcome is needs-ok (a button) and nothing stops.
Memory: in the same turn, remember with a line taken from the passage comes back as needs-ok, and memory.json is unchanged.
Echo: after B's answer quotes the passage, the same search returns A's original only, not B's answer.

Agents: a key's direct call and its ask_sparkie turn return only that agent's own conversations and none of the owner's. The owner's search finds the agent's conversation, labelled with the agent's name.

Archive (with the chat limit set to 5 by a test-only environment value): the 6th chat is created with 201, not 409. The oldest chats are lines in chats-archive.jsonl, are still found with archived: true, open with GET /chats/<id>, and refuse a new message with 409.
Delete: after DELETE on a live chat and on an archived chat, neither is found and the archive line is gone.
Restart: the same search gives the same results after the service restarts, and also after the index file is removed or filled with garbage before the start. Chats work throughout.
Query safety: a query made of FTS5 operators and quotes, such as '") OR chat: NEAR(', returns an ordinary result or none, never an error from SQLite.
No SQLite (simulated by a test-only switch): the console starts, chats save, and search answers in plain words that it needs Node.js 22.13 or newer.

On Spark 2 after the install: /health shows node 22.13 or newer, POST /actions/search_documents answers in under 100 ms, and Sparkie answers the owner's three example sentences with a date and a chat title.
The door tests' tool lists (test/lib.mjs) are unchanged by this work: it adds a source to an existing action, not a new tool.
dependsOn: knowledge-1: the index file with its one opener, and the search_documents action with a source input. If the owner wants recall first, those two pieces (about 30 lines) are built here and knowledge-1 adds its own source later.

Node.js 22.13 or newer on Spark 2, for the built-in node:sqlite with FTS5. Unknown from the repository: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/deploy/host-on-portal.sh lines 76-81 accept Node 18 and newer and may fall back to code-server's Node. Check /health's `node` field before building; if it is older, the owner updates Node once by hand.

The chat archive from the reviews' list (docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md, Memory: 'Archive old owner chats instead of the hard 300 limit'). It is not built yet, so step 1 builds it here; if another batch builds it first, step 1 drops out.

The usual release path: node tools/build-server.mjs, then node test/lock.mjs, then the installer. The planned gate image is Node 24, which has node:sqlite without a flag (it prints one 'experimental' warning line).
Does not depend on knowledge-4 (vectors), any container, or the brain's setup. Vectors are worth adding later only if keyword search is seen to miss in real use.

Sources opened for this check: sqlite.org/fts5.html, nodejs.org/api/sqlite.html, Node's deps/sqlite/sqlite.gyp on the v22.x and v24.x branches, github.com/tobi/qmd, arxiv.org/abs/2605.15184 and arxiv.org/abs/2410.10813. The session's web search limit was reached before the LongMemEval lookup, so that one was confirmed from its arXiv page directly. qmd's README does not state Linux ARM64 support, which does not matter here because qmd is not installed.

problems: The index is not needed at this size, and it brings a runtime dependency on the hub. The designer's facts hold (FTS5 is compiled into Node 22.x and 24.x; no flag from 22.13), but node:sqlite is still marked 'Stability 1.1, active development' there. The installer accepts Node 18 and newer and may fall back to code-server's copy (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/deploy/host-on-portal.sh:76-81), and Ubuntu 24.04's packaged Node is 18. The gate image is Node 24, so the gate would pass while Spark 2 runs with search off. The 'one-time owner step' is replacing the Node that runs the console (system-wide, with the path pinned in the unit): the one process that must not break, for a small feature. Measured here in memory (Node 26.6, arm64, 20,000 messages, 12 MB): FTS5 build 253 ms synchronous, FTS5 query about 10 ms, a plain scan for three words about 7 ms. All live chats are already in memory (chatData()).

A synchronous write inside saveChats() sits on the product's hottest path. saveChats is called from about ten places (every message, every finished answer, every operation notice, every button state: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs:24, 84, 111, 127, 195, 203). The try/catch keeps chat alive but hides index errors, so the index can drift until the next restart, and Sparkie then says 'we never discussed that' when you did. A scan of the live data cannot drift and needs no rebuild at start.

Agent scoping fails open. The filter depends on ctx.agentId being added at two call sites. Other paths reach actions with no agent identity: a saved workflow's steps run as {via:'workflow'} even when an agent started the workflow (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/18-workflows.mjs:193), and saved workflows may contain any action as a step. Any path that forgets the id gets the owner's view. With scope 'fleet:read' the tool is also listed to every read-only agent key at /mcp (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-mcp.mjs:156). It must be the other way round: owner's chats only when the caller is provably the owner.

Letting the owner's search return agents' conversations lets outside text pose as a past decision. An agent (or a web page an agent relayed) can write 'the owner decided X' into its ask_sparkie conversation; Sparkie's reply in that conversation may repeat it and would be labelled as Sparkie's. Recall then presents it in the owner's chat. The gate still stops changes (it reads only ctx.said, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/16-actions.mjs:250-262), but the answer is wrong and the owner may act on it. The same applies, more weakly, to Sparkie's own old answers, which paraphrase web pages, recipes and logs: a 'who said it' label is not enough unless the owner's own words rank first and 'decided' means the owner said or agreed to it.

'Plus the message before and after' brings back what the design promises to exclude. In a real chat the neighbour of an owner message is often an operation notice that quotes program output (14-chats.mjs:125) or an automatic carry-on prompt (14-chats.mjs:143). The exclusion has to apply to neighbours too, not only to what is matched.

The archive is the only step that can lose the owner's chats, and its guard is thin. An append that is cut short (disk full) leaves a broken last line; the chat is then dropped from chats.json and exists only in yesterday's backup. DELETE on an archived chat rewrites the whole file, and a rewrite that skips lines it cannot parse loses more. A chat archived while it has a running operation or a carry-on task loses its result, because postResult returns silently when the conversation is not found (14-chats.mjs:117-118). ownChat() serves five routes (GET, rename, delete, messages, choose: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/24-handler.mjs:579-618), each of which needs the archive case.

Archived chats vanish from the page without a word. The page lists only what GET /chats returns (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/public/app.js:391, and its own 'Search chats' box at 3651 filters that list), so a moved chat looks deleted. 'Quietly' is right for notifications but wrong for the list.

'Deleting means gone' promises more than is true. A deleted chat stays in up to 14 daily state copies on another Spark (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/25-backup-and-start.mjs:12-13, which tars the whole state folder) and in installer snapshots. An index file in that folder would add a third place: SQLite's free pages keep dropped text, and the file would be copied daily, sometimes mid-write. 'Nothing new to back up' is not what the tar does.

It depends on two things that do not exist. Neither search_documents nor knowledge-1's index file is in the code. The acceptance line 'tool lists unchanged' is true only if knowledge-1 ships first; otherwise this is a 37th tool, against the 36-tool ceiling the tools analysis proposes for the 27B brain (/Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/docs/analysis-2026-11-11/02-tools-and-freshness.md:166). With the archive, five routes, the index, the save hook, the ctx changes, a new message flag and 14 acceptance checks, the effort is M, not S.

The echo guard throws away real content and adds state that is not needed. Marking every answer from a recall turn as never searchable also hides new proposals made in that turn. The saved answer already records which tools ran (message.tools, 14-chats.mjs:337-338), so no 'recalled' flag is needed; those answers can simply rank below the originals.

Old numbers pass as checked, and the size limit is measured in the wrong place. unsupportedNumbers() counts every tool result as a source (14-chats.mjs:336), so a speed or size quoted from a month-old chat shows as tool-backed today. The 10,000-character budget is counted before JSON encoding; passages full of commands, quotes and line breaks grow when encoded and can cross Sparkie's 12,000 cut (14-chats.mjs:314), which chops the result mid-passage.

Not a fault today, but it becomes a leak with the messaging the owner asked for. Once Sparkie answers over Telegram or iMessage, a recall answer sends old chat text to an outside service, and maskSecrets() only knows common token shapes, not a password written in a sentence.
attack.smallerVersion: One read action, search_chats, with no SQLite: it scans the owner's own chats already in memory (chatData()) for 2 to 5 key words, in the owner's messages and Sparkie's answers only, owner's words ranked first, and returns up to 5 dated, masked passages. Owner-only: a scope no agent key holds, refused when ctx.agent is set or a workflow calls it; agents' conversations are not searched. No index, no save hook, no Node upgrade. Separately, the archive: at the limit, write the 20 oldest idle chats to chats-archive.jsonl, read them back, and only then drop them; search reads the archive only when live chats give under 3 passages. Move to FTS5 only if a search passes 100 ms.
mustHaveGuards: Fail closed on who is asking. The owner's chats are searched only when the call is the owner's page, the owner's POST /actions call, or Sparkie in the owner's own chat (via 'sparkie' and ctx.agent false). Everything else is refused in plain words: agents at /mcp, Sparkie answering an agent, saved-workflow steps, healing, the gateway. The action has its own scope that agent keys never receive, so it is not listed at /mcp. Tests: an agent key's tools/list does not show it; an ask_sparkie turn and a run_workflow step are both refused.

Search can never break chat. It reads chatData() at query time. Nothing is added to saveChats(), no index file, no node:sqlite, no work at start-up. If search throws, creating and saving chats behave exactly as today.

Only prose is matched or shown: the owner's messages and Sparkie's answers. Never operation notices, button outcomes, carry-on prompts, failed answers, page snapshots (the context field), members' chats or agents' conversations. The same rule applies to the neighbouring messages shown round a match.

Every passage carries who said it, the date, days ago and the chat's title, plus one note: this is what was said then, not the state now. The owner's own messages rank above Sparkie's. The prompt sentence says a decision is only what the owner said or agreed to, and that what is live wins.

Recalled text stays data. The action stays out of INSIDE_READS, so the turn counts as having read outside text, and the gate keeps reading only ctx.said. Tests: an old 'stop gemma on spark 3' line cannot make a stop run (it comes back as a button), and a remember built from a passage comes back as a button with memory.json unchanged.

Secrets: every passage goes through maskSecrets() before it is returned, on every path including POST /actions. A match whose word falls inside a hidden span is dropped, so a pasted token cannot be found by searching for it. The query is written nowhere except the existing masked audit line.

The archive never loses a chat. Write the archive to a temporary file and rename it (or append, then read the new lines back and parse them) before anything leaves chats.json. Never archive a chat that is being answered, has a running operation, a carry-on task or open buttons. Any rewrite keeps lines it cannot parse byte for byte. A chat found in both places resolves to the live copy. The file is 0600. Test with a simulated short write: the chat is still in chats.json.

Archived chats stay visible and deletable. GET /chats reports how many are archived and the page shows one line ('N older chats are archived; ask Sparkie to find them'). GET and DELETE by id work on the archive with the passkey as today; sending a message, pressing a button or renaming answers 409 in plain words.
Say the truth about deleting: a deleted chat is gone from search at once (nothing is indexed), and the daily copies on the other Spark keep it for up to 14 days. No stronger promise than that.

Bounded and quick. Query up to 200 characters and 12 words; at most 5 passages; at most 9,000 characters measured after JSON encoding. The scan yields to other work every 50 chats and the archive is read as a stream. Test: under 50 ms on 20 MB of chat text.

No echo, with no new flag: an answer whose saved tools list includes search_chats is not a match target (or ranks last), using the existing message.tools record. In the current chat, the last 20 messages are skipped because Sparkie already has them.

One tool, counted inside Sparkie's ceiling of 36. If search_documents is built later, this becomes its 'chats' source with every guard above unchanged; FTS5 is considered only then, and only if a search is measured over 100 ms.
If a messaging channel (Telegram, iMessage, SMS) is added later, recall is off on that channel until the owner turns it on from the passkey-signed page.

Nothing new is exposed or spent: no container, port, download, model, GPU, token, notification or extra brain turn. The change stays inside /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/14-chats.mjs (prompt sentence), a new small part beside /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-memory.mjs (the action), /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/24-handler.mjs (archive at the limit; GET and DELETE fall back), /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/lib.mjs with a new test file, and one line in /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/public/app.js. Nothing in sign-in, deploy, SSH or Tailscale files.

design.title: Ask Sparkie from the Action Button or "Hey Siri": one Shortcut and a plain-text door (/say)
design.design:
Paths are under /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console. Nothing new runs on the Sparks: no container, port, GPU or download, so ARM64 does not apply. Outside pieces: the iPhone's Shortcuts app (Dictate Text, Get Contents of URL, Get Dictionary Value, Speak Text), Siri, and the Action Button.

1. The door, in service/src/20-mcp.mjs: `POST /console/api/say {text, wait?}` answers a flat `{status, say, ask, conversation}`. `sayDoor` (about 45 lines beside `mcpDoor`: same key check, JSON-only rule, limits, audit) calls `askSparkie`, which gains two options: `waitMs` (8 s here, 40 s as before for MCP) and `plain`.
2. One rolling conversation per key: the key's newest conversation marked `say`, reused if used in the last 30 minutes, still answering, or holding an open question. Empty `text` returns what arrived since the last ask. No new state file.
3. Two pure helpers there: `heard()` ("spark three" becomes "spark 3"; "Yes, do it." reads as yes) and `spoken()` (strips markdown, ids and addresses, cuts at a sentence near 500 characters, adds "The rest is in the chat.").
4. service/src/24-handler.mjs: accept a key without Tailscale on `/say` (line 81), route it beside `/mcp` (line 102), give its errors a `say` field, and let `POST /agents` take `door: "say"`. `keyViewer` and `agentFor` refuse such a key anywhere but `/say`.
5. service/src/14-chats.mjs: on a plain turn `systemPrompt` replaces the "you are talking with an agent" line (line 51) with a spoken-style line (two short sentences, no markdown or ids, one yes/no question when unsure) and includes memory (line 54).
6. service/src/16-actions.mjs `runAction` (line 302): on a plain turn every change except `remember` is proposed, never run at once; `ask` is the console's own button label.
7. public/app.js `connectAgent` (line 4706): a "Phone (Siri or a Shortcut)" choice showing the address, the key and the Shortcut steps.
8. docs/contract.md (sections 13 and 4), docs/agent-door.md, a new test/say.test.mjs, one case in test/internet.test.mjs.

Data, not code: the Shortcut, the key's hash and `door` in agents.json, the conversations in chats.json. Code: about 100 lines plus tests.
design.ownerExperience:
